subject.title: [Feature]: Fallback approval mode + model attribution in messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in approval gate before executing configured model fallbacks, and should that be per-agent config, per-session state, or an extension/approval event contract?
rationale: The remaining request changes fallback runtime behavior and adds a config/control surface; repository policy treats fallback behavior, provider routing, and new config as product- and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Design Core Default-Off Gate
options.body: Define a per-agent or inherited default-off approval policy with timeout behavior, no-route behavior, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep Automatic Failover
options.body: Treat fallback notices, status, logs, and response-prefix attribution as the supported control/visibility model and close this direction as not planned.

options.title: Design Extension Hook First
options.body: Add or reuse an approval/event seam so plugins or operators can own fallback approval policy without a one-off model config key.

recommendation.title: Design Core Default-Off Gate
recommendation.body: Define a per-agent or inherited default-off approval policy with timeout behavior, no-route behavior, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Fallback policy history and current product-boundary evidence route this decision most strongly to steipete.
